commits.message: refactor(skills): rebuild repo skills around setup, doctor, and real paths
commits.message_full:
refactor(skills): rebuild repo skills around setup, doctor, and real paths

Most skill paths pointed at `src/...` locations that moved into
`apps/web`, `packages/config`, and `packages/i18n`. Two skills still
taught the removed placeholder pattern. Claude Code could not discover
the skills because there was no `.claude/skills`.

- Nine task skills replace the old eight: musemvp-setup,
  musemvp-connect-services, musemvp-new-feature, musemvp-customize-site,
  musemvp-customize-app, musemvp-testing, musemvp-review, musemvp-deploy,
  musemvp-changelog. The router skill is gone; AGENTS.md holds the
  routing table.
- New skills build on muse:init and muse:doctor, separate human-only
  steps from agent steps, and cover Dodo via MCP, mail, OAuth, Turnstile,
  storage, and deployment.
- `scripts/skills.ts` checks frontmatter, size, every referenced path,
  skill cross-references, the AGENTS.md index, and the `.claude/skills`
  copy. `pnpm skills:sync` regenerates the copy (copies, not symlinks,
  for Windows). `pnpm skills:check` runs in CI.

Refs musemvp/musemvp-com#28

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: ci: replay a new buyer's first run for both apps
commits.message_full:
ci: replay a new buyer's first run for both apps

Two jobs start from a clean checkout with no third-party keys: init,
doctor, a dev server, then scripts/first-run-smoke.mjs (seed sign-in,
closed password sign-up, email-code sign-up through console mail, dev
origin rules). The Node job runs against a Postgres service and also runs
the full API contract suite, which CI did not run before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: docs: add the new-buyer guide and align setup docs
commits.message_full:
docs: add the new-buyer guide and align setup docs

docs/getting-started.zh.md walks a buyer from a fresh clone to production:
choosing an app, the three setup commands, what works locally without
keys, prompts for AI agents, connecting payments, mail, OAuth, Turnstile,
and storage, recommended MCP servers, and a table of every step that
needs a human. README, AGENTS.md, and skills now use the new init and
doctor commands. The billing module README no longer claims gateway
credentials come from app settings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: feat(cli): require --app for init and report per-app status in doctor
commits.message_full:
feat(cli): require --app for init and report per-app status in doctor

`pnpm muse:init` now takes `--app cloudflare|node|both` and finishes the
whole local setup: env file, migrations, seed accounts, and the right
next command. It edits `.env.local` in place, so re-running it keeps
values, comments, and custom keys. It records the app in the gitignored
`muse.project.json` and prints short errors with the next command
instead of stack traces. `--docker` waits for the Postgres health check.

`pnpm muse:doctor` checks only the chosen app and reports each feature as
ready, local, disabled, or missing, with the variable names involved and
a fix. `--json` is for agents, never includes env values, and exits 1
when a blocking check fails. The Cloudflare app is no longer told it
needs DATABASE_URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: fix(mail): print mail locally when MAIL_PROVIDER is empty
commits.message_full:
fix(mail): print mail locally when MAIL_PROVIDER is empty

The example and init used console mail, but an empty MAIL_PROVIDER fell
back to Resend at runtime. An empty value now means console outside
production and the platform provider (Resend or Cloudflare) in
production. The Cloudflare app also supports MAIL_PROVIDER=console in
development, so sign-up codes reach the dev server terminal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: feat(dev): trust localhost on any port outside production
commits.message_full:
feat(dev): trust localhost on any port outside production

Next.js moves to the next free port when 3000 is taken, and the auth
origin check then rejected sign-in from that port. Outside production,
Better Auth and the API CORS check now accept http://localhost and
http://127.0.0.1 on any port. Production keeps the exact origin list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: fix(auth): close the password sign-up endpoint
commits.message_full:
fix(auth): close the password sign-up endpoint

`config.auth.gates.allowRegister: false` hid the register page but left
POST /api/auth/sign-up/email open. With the gate closed, Better Auth also
turned on autoSignIn and turned off email verification, so anyone could
create an account with an unverified address and get a session.

Accounts are created through email OTP, which proves the address, so the
password sign-up endpoint now stays closed whatever the gate says. Password
sign-in still works for seeded and admin-created users, and never signs in
an unverified address. Test helpers create password users directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
